body:
I'm not sure this would actually work in the context of multithreaded rendering, because I think the managed thread on the Java side may be a different OS thread than the C++ thread making this call. So, we may need to completely move the `eglMakeCurrent()` to the C++ side, rather than making a JNI call to do it on the Java side

I'll need to test this, though :-)

The Java logic is run on the caller thread unless a call to `runOnHostThread` is done. So this should work as expected.

You can validate by having logcat display the thread when printing log statements.
Why does this always pass `null` as the surface?
Same question here: why always pass `null` as the surface?
Ah, yeah, you're right, this does seem to be the case
Historically, it's because the native Android OpenGL logic didn't make use of the Android surface given that most of the OpenGL setup was done in the Java layer.
